title: Natural Neural Structure in Artificial Neural Networks

So first, let's talk about what we mean by natural neural structure. One way to talk about structure or any type of bias in a system is an inductive bias. And so an inductive bias can loosely be defined as an a priori restriction of a set of realizable hypotheses when you're doing model selection. More colloquially, we can call this something like before seeing any data, it's a restriction of what and how you can learn. So very broadly, this can include anything from model class to optimization procedures or even hyperparameters. And in some sense, they really define what is possible to learn. So what we mean by natural inductive biases then is biases that stem from the restrictions and limitations that are faced by natural systems, by the nature of having to live in the real world.
